Nitrate in groundwater

Part of southern England

This map shows nitrate concentrations in groundwater across southern England. Each dot is a monitoring well, and its colour shows the median nitrate level measured there over the past five years. Wells on chalk bedrock consistently show higher nitrate than wells on clay, particularly where the surrounding land is intensively farmed.

Click any dot to see its reading. The Legend tab explains the colours, and the box at the top of the map switches layers on and off.

Key finding

One in five chalk wells exceeds the drinking-water limit. No clay well does. Wells surrounded by farmland show higher nitrate than those that are not.

How the map was made

Nitrate results were pulled from the Environment Agency archive for groundwater wells in the study area. Each well was assigned to an aquifer type using the British Geological Survey bedrock map. Source Protection Zones and farmland – cropland plus grassland from satellite imagery – were overlaid to test whether they relate to nitrate levels.

Limitations

  • The aquifer type is based on bedrock at the surface. The actual depth a well draws from is not recorded, so some wells near geological boundaries may be misclassified.
  • The clay median of 0.10 milligrams per litre is at the detection limit: most clay wells are simply non-detect rather than low.
  • Farmland is a 2021 snapshot. Nitrate reaching a chalk well today may reflect land use from decades earlier.
  • No statistical significance testing was performed.

Data sources

  • Environment Agency Water Quality Archive – nitrate measurements, 2021–2026. Open Government Licence.

Terms used

Nitrate as Nitrogen
The form reported by the Environment Agency, in milligrams per litre.
Drinking-water limit
11.3 milligrams per litre as Nitrogen, equivalent to 50 milligrams per litre as Nitrate.
Source Protection Zone
A regulatory zone around a drinking-water abstraction point, defined by groundwater travel time.
Chalk
A highly permeable limestone aquifer.
Clay / low-permeability
Formations that restrict groundwater flow.
